Which Yosys command maps the combinational logic into 4-input LUTs?

A) abc -lut 4

B) stat -lut 4

C) dfflibmap -lut 4

D) techmap -lut 4
problems.a: abc -lut 4
problems.e: abc -lut k asks ABC to map the logic into k-input LUTs.

What does Yosys's techmap command do in general?

A) It replaces cells with implementations taken from a map file written in Verilog

B) It sizes gates for timing

C) It places cells in rows

D) It runs ABC on the design
problems.a: It replaces cells with implementations taken from a map file written in Verilog

A) There is no direct match; the flow first legalizes the flip-flop types to ones the library has, adding logic around them

B) ABC maps the flip-flop instead

C) dfflibmap maps it to a latch

D) The reset is silently dropped

A) To check equivalence against the library

B) To map the design onto the library

C) To import the library cells as black-box modules so later passes recognize them

D) To run static timing
problems.a: To import the library cells as black-box modules so later passes recognize them

A) A limit of 1000 cells

B) A die size of 1000 microns

C) A delay target of 1000 ps for the mapping

D) A clock skew of 1000 ps
problems.a: A delay target of 1000 ps for the mapping
problems.e: -D sets the delay target, which steers ABC's mapping and its timing-driven optimizations.

problems.q:
Why does a Yosys flow map flip-flops with dfflibmap before running abc?

A) Because the order does not matter in any flow

B) So ABC sees the flip-flops as fixed library cells and maps only the combinational logic between them

C) Because dfflibmap needs ABC's output

D) Because abc deletes unmapped flip-flops
problems.a: So ABC sees the flip-flops as fixed library cells and maps only the combinational logic between them
problems.e: With flip-flops already mapped, ABC treats their pins as the boundary of the combinational logic it optimizes.

After Yosys maps with abc, which independent check should a flow run before trusting the netlist?

A) stat with -liberty

B) A lint check of the Liberty file

C) A second abc run with the same settings

D) An equivalence check between the pre-mapping and post-mapping designs
problems.a: An equivalence check between the pre-mapping and post-mapping designs
problems.e: Equivalence checking proves the mapped netlist implements the same function, independent of the tool that produced it.

problems.q:
An engineer swaps 'abc -liberty' for a hand-written techmap file that maps each AND gate to a NAND2 plus INV. What is lost?

A) Covering: one-to-one substitution cannot choose larger cells or trade area against delay

B) Logical correctness

C) Flip-flop mapping

D) The ability to read Liberty files
problems.a: Covering: one-to-one substitution cannot choose larger cells or trade area against delay
problems.e: techmap substitutes cells by rule. ABC's mapper solves a covering problem with costs, which is where the quality comes from.

label: A match-cost seam for library-specific mapping
lesson:
# A match-cost seam for library-specific mapping

In an agent-first mapper, the covering algorithm is fixed, but how a match is priced varies by customer, library and objective. The design move is a seam where the dynamic program asks one question: what does this match cost in this context? Placing that seam well lets agents and users change mapping behaviour at the configuration or plug-in tier without touching cut enumeration, matching or legality.

## Core versus change surface in a mapper

The immutable core of a mapper guarantees a legal, equivalent cover: AIG construction, cut enumeration, canonicalization and Boolean matching, the covering DP and cover selection. The change surface is everything that only ranks legal choices: area and delay weights, per-cell penalties, don't-use lists, power terms, load estimates. A cost-provider interface separates the two. The core enumerates the legal matches at a node and calls the provider once, coarsely, with the batch; the provider returns a cost for each. Cost policy can then never break equivalence, because it never decides what is legal.

## What the seam's context must carry

A provider can only express policies its context supports. Useful context for a match: the cell and its drive strength and Vt class, the pin assignment from the matching transformation, input arrival times, the estimated load and required time at the node, the node's estimated fanout, and the mapping pass (delay, area flow, exact area). With that, a request such as "penalize high-Vt cells on paths with less than 50 ps slack" is a small plug-in that reads slack and Vt class. Leave out layout code, global state and anything nondeterministic, so plug-ins stay testable and reproducible.

## Keeping the seam honest

Three rules keep a cost seam safe. Costs rank and never forbid: legality constraints, such as forbidding matches across a clock-gating boundary, need a separate match-filter seam, because a huge cost still loses to nothing when no alternative exists. The interface is narrow and frozen, so plug-ins compile separately and can be swapped by configuration, for example a fast linear delay model during exploration and a Liberty-table model for the final pass. Every provider ships with golden tests: equivalence of the mapped netlist plus a differential QoR report showing that the matches that changed are the ones the policy targets.

## Going deeper

The OpenROAD and ABC source code for examples of cost hooks in mapping and sizing; Gamma, Helm, Johnson and Vlissides, "Design Patterns" (1994), for the strategy pattern behind provider seams.

problems.q:
Where should a library-specific cost function plug into a cut-based mapper?

A) Inside the cut enumeration loop, as an edit to the merge code

B) In the equivalence checker

C) In the Liberty parser

D) At the point where the DP asks for the cost of a match: a cost-provider interface called with the match context
problems.a: At the point where the DP asks for the cost of a match: a cost-provider interface called with the match context
problems.e: The DP asks one question per candidate match. Putting the seam there lets cost policies change without touching enumeration or matching.

problems.q:
In a mapping engine, which part belongs in the immutable core rather than behind a seam?

A) Cut enumeration, matching and the covering dynamic program, which guarantee a legal, equivalent cover

B) The choice of which library cells to exclude

C) The weights that trade area against delay

D) The per-cell cost adjustments a customer requests
problems.a: Cut enumeration, matching and the covering dynamic program, which guarantee a legal, equivalent cover
problems.e: Correctness of the cover lives in the core. The costs that rank legal matches vary by customer and belong at a seam.

problems.q:
A match-cost seam receives a context. Which item is least useful to include in it?

A) The source code of the cell's layout generator

B) The cell and its Vt class

C) The arrival times of the match's inputs

D) The estimated load and required time at the node
problems.a: The source code of the cell's layout generator
problems.e: A cost provider ranks matches by area, delay, power and slack. It needs the cell, timing context and load estimate, not layout code.

problems.q:
A new cost provider makes the mapper choose different cells, but the mapped netlist fails equivalence. What does this indicate?

A) Equivalence checking is too strict for mapping

B) The cost provider is working as intended

C) The library is incomplete

D) The seam leaks: cost policy was able to affect legality, which the core should guarantee regardless of cost
problems.a: The seam leaks: cost policy was able to affect legality, which the core should guarantee regardless of cost
problems.e: Costs should only rank legal matches. If a cost change breaks equivalence, the core let policy decide something it must own.

problems.q:
What must the cost seam's interface be, to let plug-ins be compiled separately and swapped safely?

A) Wide, exposing all internal data structures

B) Based on parsing log files

C) Changed every release to add features

D) Narrow and stable: plain data in, cost numbers out, no hidden global state
problems.a: Narrow and stable: plain data in, cost numbers out, no hidden global state
problems.e: A frozen, narrow interface is what lets plug-ins be developed, tested and replaced without recompiling the core.

problems.q:
What must the cost seam's interface be, to let plug-ins be compiled separately and swapped safely?

A) Changed every release to add features

B) Narrow and stable: plain data in, cost numbers out, no hidden global state

C) Based on parsing log files

D) Wide, exposing all internal data structures
problems.a: Narrow and stable: plain data in, cost numbers out, no hidden global state
problems.e: A frozen, narrow interface is what lets plug-ins be developed, tested and replaced without recompiling the core.

problems.q:
A team wants a cost provider that calls a learned power model. What is the main risk to manage at the seam?

A) It cannot return numbers

B) It changes the subject graph

C) The model's latency and accuracy: it is called for many matches, and its errors steer the mapper

D) It forbids area recovery
problems.a: The model's latency and accuracy: it is called for many matches, and its errors steer the mapper
problems.e: A seam can host a learned model, but the call volume and the model's error both feed directly into covering decisions.

problems.q:
Which test proves a new cost provider did what was intended?

A) A clean compile

B) A shorter log file

C) A larger number of cuts enumerated

D) Equivalence plus a differential QoR report showing that the changed matches are the ones the policy targets
problems.a: Equivalence plus a differential QoR report showing that the changed matches are the ones the policy targets
problems.e: Equivalence shows the cover is legal; the differential report shows the policy moved the intended decisions and nothing else.

problems.q:
Mapping should use different delay models for the early fast pass and the final pass. How should the engine support this?

A) Two implementations of the same delay-model interface, chosen by configuration

B) An if-statement on the design name inside the DP

C) Two copies of the mapper core

D) Editing the Liberty file between passes
problems.a: Two implementations of the same delay-model interface, chosen by configuration
problems.e: One seam with interchangeable providers lets a fast model and an accurate model coexist, selected without code edits.

label: Agents choosing mapping recipes
prereqs: Required depths and LUT area recovery
lesson:
# Agents choosing mapping recipes

Most mapping wins in practice come not from new algorithms but from choosing the right script: which mapper, which K, whether to compute choices, how many area-recovery passes. An agent can make that choice from manifests and measured QoR, if the recipes are packaged as skills with honest descriptions and the loop is grounded in reference engines rather than proxies.

## Recipes as skills with manifests

Package each mapping recipe as a skill: the script, its build and dependencies, golden tests, and a short manifest stating the target (LUT or standard cell), objective (depth-first, delay-first with area recovery, area-only), inputs and outputs, tunable parameters (K, priority cuts per node, delay target, number of recovery passes), and known strengths and weaknesses. The agent selects by reading manifests, a cheap text decision: an FPGA target excludes standard-cell recipes, a failing timing report points to a delay-first recipe, and a hard area cap points to area-oriented ones.

## Running and comparing candidates

An agent can run several recipes in parallel and keep the best, but only among valid results: each candidate must pass equivalence checking and meet the timing constraint before area is compared, and all must run on the same design, library and constraints. Fast estimates, such as the mapper's own depth and area or a quick timer, filter recipes cheaply; the reference timer, ideally after placement, decides. The loop needs a stopping rule, an iteration budget and a minimum improvement, or it oscillates between recipes that each fix what the other broke.

## Learning which recipe to pick

Each run is data: design features (size, depth, fanout distribution, datapath versus control), recipe, parameters and measured QoR. Recording when a recipe wins, in its manifest and in the domain model, is the skill flywheel: the next selection starts from experience. Rewards for learned selection must use the real objectives measured by reference engines. A reward on cell count alone invites recipes that use few large cells and hurt area and delay; a reward on the mapper's own delay estimate invites results that collapse after placement. Tool-grounded rewards measure what signoff will measure.

## Going deeper

The ABC and Yosys documentation for the commands recipes are built from; Mishchenko et al., "Combinational and sequential mapping with priority cuts", ICCAD 2007, for the parameters a recipe exposes.

problems.q:
Which manifest field matters most for an agent deciding whether a recipe can run on a block with a strict area cap?

A) The size of the binary

B) The objective it optimizes and the parameters that trade area for delay

C) The author's name

D) The date it was compiled
problems.a: The objective it optimizes and the parameters that trade area for delay
problems.e: The agent matches objectives and tunables to the block's constraint.

problems.q:
A block has 200 ps of negative slack after mapping with the area recipe. Which recipe should the agent try next?

A) The delay-oriented recipe with area recovery

B) The same area recipe with a different seed only

C) The LUT recipe

D) No mapping, keeping the AIG
problems.a: The delay-oriented recipe with area recovery
problems.e: The metric that is failing, timing, decides the next skill. A delay-first mapper with area recovery addresses it directly.

A block has 200 ps of negative slack after mapping with the area recipe. Which recipe should the agent try next?

A) The same area recipe with a different seed only

C) The LUT recipe

D) The delay-oriented recipe with area recovery
problems.a: The delay-oriented recipe with area recovery
problems.e: The metric that is failing, timing, decides the next skill. A delay-first mapper with area recovery addresses it directly.

A) Nowhere, since agents rediscover it

B) In a comment inside the mapper's core loop

C) By deleting the recipe

D) In the recipe's manifest and the domain model, as a condition for when to select it
problems.a: In the recipe's manifest and the domain model, as a condition for when to select it
problems.e: The flywheel captures when a skill works, so the next selection uses that knowledge.

A) A larger cut size

B) A stopping rule based on QoR progress and an iteration budget

C) More recipes to alternate between

D) A random restart each iteration
problems.a: A stopping rule based on QoR progress and an iteration budget
problems.e: Agentic loops need termination criteria; otherwise they oscillate without converging.

A recipe works well on datapath-heavy blocks and poorly on control logic. How should this knowledge be recorded?

A) By deleting the recipe

B) In the recipe's manifest and the domain model, as a condition for when to select it

C) Nowhere, since agents rediscover it

D) In a comment inside the mapper's core loop
problems.a: In the recipe's manifest and the domain model, as a condition for when to select it
problems.e: The flywheel captures when a skill works, so the next selection uses that knowledge.

A customer asks for 'smaller area at the same speed'. Which step comes first for the agent?

A) Measure the current area and delay with the reference flow to fix the baseline

B) Edit the mapper core

C) Increase K for the LUT mapper

D) Pick the area-only recipe immediately
problems.a: Measure the current area and delay with the reference flow to fix the baseline
problems.e: A delta needs a baseline; without one the agent cannot prove it met the request.

A customer asks for 'smaller area at the same speed'. Which step comes first for the agent?

A) Pick the area-only recipe immediately

B) Measure the current area and delay with the reference flow to fix the baseline

C) Edit the mapper core

D) Increase K for the LUT mapper
problems.a: Measure the current area and delay with the reference flow to fix the baseline
problems.e: A delta needs a baseline; without one the agent cannot prove it met the request.

Why should an agent try a fast mapping estimate before an accurate mapping-plus-timing run?

A) Agents cannot call timers

B) Accurate runs cannot be automated

C) The fast estimate filters recipes cheaply, and only promising ones pay for the accurate run

D) Fast estimates are always more accurate
problems.a: The fast estimate filters recipes cheaply, and only promising ones pay for the accurate run
problems.e: Fast and accurate engines work as a pair: the fast one prunes the search, the accurate one decides.

label: Equivalence and QoR deltas as golden tests
lesson:
# Equivalence and QoR deltas as golden tests

When agents edit mapping code or cost functions, every change needs an automatic, trustworthy verdict. For mapping that verdict has two parts: the mapped netlist must be equivalent to its input, and its quality must not regress beyond agreed budgets on a fixed suite of designs. Getting the order, the baseline and the statistics right is what makes the harness safe to automate.

## Equivalence before quality

Run a combinational equivalence check (ABC's cec, or a SAT-based checker) between the pre-mapping network and the mapped netlist, on every design in the suite. Only a proved result passes. A counterexample means the change is wrong, whatever its QoR. A timeout is not a pass: hold the change, rerun with more effort or another method, and keep the gate closed. Then apply the QoR rule, for example: delay may regress by at most 1 percent and area must not grow unless delay improves. A candidate with area -6.8 percent and delay +3.1 percent fails that rule on delay.

## Computing and reporting deltas

Report each design's percentage change, (candidate - baseline) / baseline x 100, and summarize with the mean of the per-design percentages (or a geometric mean of ratios), so one large design does not dominate. For areas 1041 to 1061, 826 to 821 and 1614 to 1559, the changes are +1.92, -0.61 and -3.41 percent, mean -0.70 percent. Always show the per-design list next to the mean: a 2 percent mean gain can hide one design that got 9 percent worse. Measure delay with the reference timer on the mapped netlist, not the mapper's internal estimate.

## What makes a golden suite trustworthy

The baseline is the currently promoted recipe on the same designs, library and constraints; nothing else may differ. Runs must be deterministic and seeded, or noise looks like progress. Run time and memory are tracked metrics with their own budgets, since they are part of a tool's QoR. A targeted change should have a targeted effect: if only one cell class's cost changed, the differential report should show only matches involving that class moving. Designs are never removed from the suite to make a change pass; outliers are investigated, and a real regression on one design blocks promotion until it is understood.

## Going deeper

Brayton and Mishchenko, "ABC: an academic industrial-strength verification tool", CAV 2010, for cec; the EPFL combinational benchmark suite, a standard golden set for mapping QoR.

problems.q:
An agent proposes a new mapping cost function. On the reference design the baseline mapping has area 1545 and critical delay 488 ps; the candidate gives area 1543 and delay 500 ps. The equivalence check of candidate against the pre-mapping network returned: timeout. The promotion rule is: equivalence must be proved, delay may regress by at most 3%, and area must not grow unless delay improves. What is the verdict?

A) Reject: the delay regression exceeds the budget

B) Promote: equivalent, delay within budget, area not worse

C) Reject: the mapped netlist is not equivalent

D) Hold: equivalence is unproven, so the QoR numbers cannot be trusted yet
problems.a: Hold: equivalence is unproven, so the QoR numbers cannot be trusted yet
problems.e: Equivalence comes first: QoR deltas of a wrong netlist mean nothing. Here the check timeout, area changed by -0.13% and delay by 2.46%, so the rule gives this verdict.

problems.q:

The equivalence check of candidate against the pre-mapping network returned: proved. The promotion rule is: equivalence must be proved, delay may regress by at most 1%, and area must not grow unless delay improves. What is the verdict?

A) Reject: the mapped netlist is not equivalent

B) Promote: equivalent, delay within budget, area not worse

C) Reject: the delay regression exceeds the budget

D) Hold: equivalence is unproven, so the QoR numbers cannot be trusted yet
problems.a: Reject: the delay regression exceeds the budget
problems.e: Equivalence comes first: QoR deltas of a wrong netlist mean nothing. Here the check proved, area changed by -3.08% and delay by 4.44%, so the rule gives this verdict.

The equivalence check of candidate against the pre-mapping network returned: proved. The promotion rule is: equivalence must be proved, delay may regress by at most 2%, and area must not grow unless delay improves. What is the verdict?

B) Hold: equivalence is unproven, so the QoR numbers cannot be trusted yet

problems.a: Reject: the delay regression exceeds the budget
problems.e: Equivalence comes first: QoR deltas of a wrong netlist mean nothing. Here the check proved, area changed by -1.17% and delay by 4.44%, so the rule gives this verdict.

A) -0.44

B) 0.87

C) -2.62

D) -0.87

E) 0.13

A) -1.16

B) -6.94

C) -1.31

D) 2.31

E) -2.31
problems.e: Per-design changes are -3.52, -0.33, -3.09%; their mean is -2.31%. Averaging percentages, rather than summing raw areas, keeps one large design from dominating the suite.

problems.q:
A golden QoR suite reports mapped area, baseline then candidate: design 1: 1965 -> 1847; design 2: 1097 -> 1054; design 3: 1248 -> 1207. The suite summarizes area as the mean of the per-design percentage changes. What is that mean, in percent? Negative means smaller.

A) -2.2

B) -3.4

C) -13.21

D) 4.4

E) -4.4
problems.e: Per-design changes are -6.01, -3.92, -3.29%; their mean is -4.4%. Averaging percentages, rather than summing raw areas, keeps one large design from dominating the suite.

A candidate change improves mean area by 2% on the golden suite but one design gets 9% worse. What should the differential report do?

A) Report only the mean, since it improved

B) Average the outlier with the best design

C) Show the per-design deltas and flag the outlier, rather than only the mean

D) Drop the outlier design from the suite
problems.a: Show the per-design deltas and flag the outlier, rather than only the mean
problems.e: Means hide regressions. A differential check reports where results moved, so a reviewer can see that one design was hurt.

Two runs of the same mapping change give different areas on the same design. What does this say about the golden test?

A) Equivalence checking will catch it

B) The change is good, since one run improved

C) Golden tests should take the best of several runs

D) The engine is nondeterministic, so it must be seeded and made reproducible before deltas mean anything
problems.a: The engine is nondeterministic, so it must be seeded and made reproducible before deltas mean anything
problems.e: Differential testing assumes the baseline and the candidate are each reproducible. Nondeterminism turns noise into apparent QoR changes.

problems.q:
Which check must every golden test of a mapping change include, before any QoR comparison?

A) A diff of the netlist text against the baseline

B) A comparison of run times

C) A check that the cell count did not change

D) A formal equivalence check of the mapped netlist against the input network
problems.a: A formal equivalence check of the mapped netlist against the input network
problems.e: A mapper that produces a wrong netlist can show any QoR it likes. Equivalence is the correctness gate; QoR is the quality gate.

label: Change tiers for mapping requests
prereqs: A match-cost seam for library-specific mapping
lesson:
# Change tiers for mapping requests

Requests to change a mapper arrive constantly: exclude these cells, raise K, penalize this Vt class, use our delay model, forbid matches across this boundary. Classifying each into configuration, plug-in or core edit decides who may make it, how it is verified and whether it needs a human. A well-designed mapper makes the common requests land in the first two tiers.

## Tier 1: configuration

A request that changes a value the engine already reads is Tier 1, with no recompile: a don't-use list of cells, the LUT size K, the number of priority cuts, the area-delay weight, a delay target, the number of area-recovery passes. Changing results is fine at this tier; what defines it is that no code changes. Configuration can still create infeasible problems: a don't-use list that removes every inverter leaves the library incomplete, so the engine should validate functional completeness of the remaining library before mapping.

## Tier 2: plug-ins at existing seams

A request that needs new logic, but only at an existing extension point, is Tier 2. A per-cell pin-access penalty from a customer table, a slack-dependent Vt penalty, or an in-house delay model behind the delay-model interface are all small implementations of an existing interface. They compile separately and leave the core untouched. Abusing a seam is a warning sign: implementing "forbid this match" as an enormous cost is not safe, because when no alternative exists the forbidden match still wins. That request needs a legality seam.

## Tier 3: core edits and seam design

A request that changes cut enumeration, matching, the covering DP or legality, with no seam for it, is Tier 3: a core edit with a human-approved diff and full regression. If an agent proposes a core edit for a request that a plug-in could serve, the harness steers it back to the smallest safe tier. Recurring Tier 3 requests of one kind mean a seam is missing: adding a match-filter extension point, for example, turns future legality requests into Tier 2. A seam is well placed when the common kind of change never needs a core edit, and every tier, including Tier 1, still passes equivalence and QoR golden tests.

## Going deeper

The agent_first_eda domain's treatment of change tiers and seams; the ABC source code, whose command options and plug-in points show which mapping changes are configuration today.

problems.q:
A user asks the mapping engine to exclude all cells with drive strength 1 from the library. Which change tier is this?

A) Tier 1, configuration: a don't-use list, with no recompile

B) It cannot be done

C) Tier 2, a new cost plug-in

D) Tier 3, a core edit to matching
problems.a: Tier 1, configuration: a don't-use list, with no recompile
problems.e: Excluding cells is a table or list change that the engine reads at run time.

problems.q:
A user asks for a cost that penalizes cells whose pins are hard to reach in their specific layout style, using a per-cell table they supply. Which tier?

A) No change needed

B) Tier 3, an edit to the DP

C) Tier 1, by editing the Liberty area

D) Tier 2, a cost-provider plug-in that reads the table
problems.a: Tier 2, a cost-provider plug-in that reads the table
problems.e: A new cost term computed from new data is a small implementation at the cost seam.

problems.q:
A user asks the mapping engine to exclude all cells with drive strength 1 from the library. Which change tier is this?

A) Tier 1, configuration: a don't-use list, with no recompile

B) Tier 2, a new cost plug-in

C) It cannot be done

D) Tier 3, a core edit to matching
problems.a: Tier 1, configuration: a don't-use list, with no recompile
problems.e: Excluding cells is a table or list change that the engine reads at run time.

problems.q:
A user wants matches that cross a clock-gating boundary to be forbidden. The mapper has no hook for match legality. Which tier is this, and what does it suggest?

A) Tier 3, a core edit, and it suggests the engine needs a legality seam for match filtering

B) Tier 1, a parameter

C) Tier 2, using the cost seam with an infinite cost

D) Tier 1, by deleting the clock gates
problems.a: Tier 3, a core edit, and it suggests the engine needs a legality seam for match filtering
problems.e: Legality belongs to the core. If such requests recur, a match-filter extension point should be added so they become Tier 2.

problems.q:
A user's request can be met with the cost seam by assigning an enormous cost to forbidden matches. Why is this risky?

A) If every legal alternative is also expensive or missing, the mapper may still pick a forbidden match, so legality is not guaranteed

B) Costs cannot be large

C) Large numbers slow the mapper

D) It is not risky
problems.a: If every legal alternative is also expensive or missing, the mapper may still pick a forbidden match, so legality is not guaranteed
problems.e: Costs rank; they do not forbid. Legality constraints need a mechanism that removes options.

problems.q:
A user asks for a different cut enumeration algorithm that enumerates cuts on the fly. Which tier?

A) Tier 1, a parameter

B) Tier 2, a cost plug-in

C) Tier 1, by lowering K

D) Tier 3, a core edit with human review and full regression
problems.a: Tier 3, a core edit with human review and full regression
problems.e: Cut enumeration is part of the core's search; changing it changes the engine itself.

problems.q:
Over a year, most mapping requests land in Tier 3. What does this say about the engine?

A) The engine is well designed

B) The users are asking for too much

C) The seams are in the wrong place: common changes should land at configuration or plug-in tiers

D) Tier 3 edits are the safest
problems.a: The seams are in the wrong place: common changes should land at configuration or plug-in tiers
problems.e: A seam is well placed when the common kind of change never needs a core edit.

problems.q:
Which verification should a Tier 2 mapping plug-in pass before promotion?

A) A code review of the core

B) Only a compile

C) No tests, since the core is untouched

D) Golden tests with equivalence checks plus a differential QoR comparison against the baseline
problems.a: Golden tests with equivalence checks plus a differential QoR comparison against the baseline
problems.e: Plug-ins change results, so they need the same correctness and QoR gates as any change.

problems.q:
An agent proposes a core edit to fix a Tier 2 request because it is quicker for it. What should the harness do?

A) Accept the core edit if it compiles

B) Steer it to the smallest safe tier: implement the plug-in, and require human approval for any core edit

C) Reject the request

D) Let the agent edit both
problems.a: Steer it to the smallest safe tier: implement the plug-in, and require human approval for any core edit
problems.e: The model edits at the smallest safe tier. Core edits need human-approved diffs and full regression.
